String of pulses → 5×5 MZI mesh: what it computes, and how close to attention it gets

All-silica platform, everything pinned to the silica-eo-converter FDTD calibrations (MEEP 1.29, 2D Ez). Slot rate = master-MRR FSR = 1.995 THz (slot 501.3 fs); one-slot delay = 100.53 μm of bus = exactly one ring circumference per ladder tap.

Verdict on the attention question. Feeding the mesh the same pulse train delayed by one slot per input port does not build attention — it builds exactly the attention-free token mixer (Hyena / FNet / S4 class): each output port is an FIR filter over the token sequence with kernel = one row of U; the whole operator is causal banded Toeplitz, position-dependent but content-independent. The gap is structural: attention is cubic in its input, a passive mesh is linear — no topology, delay pattern, or N fixes that. But the photodetector closes it: its square law is the missing bilinearity. Interfering the train with its own k-slot-delayed copy (λ/4 offset) in the calibrated coupler and balanced-detecting yields st·st-k — the raw QKT score band, computed at the full 2 THz line rate. That is the O(L·N) part of attention; softmax + reweighting stay electronic (the silica EO port is photon-lifetime-limited to ~0.1–1 GHz, so a data-dependent second optical pass works on ~2000-slot frames, not per slot).

1 · Architecture

The mesh is the standard Clements rectangle; every node is the FDTD-calibrated silica MZI (couplers gap 0.30 μm, LC=5.35 μm with s-bends, phase electrodes on straight arms). The decomposition is run natively on the measured coupler angle κ=0.7368 (45/55 split): the Clements nulling conditions only need the ratio |B|/|A|, which the imperfect node still spans, and the diagonal-sweep identity survives by unitarity — so no global optimization and no per-node trim iteration is needed. Residual mesh error is dominated by differential path loss (edge modes traverse fewer lossy MZIs), not by the coupler imbalance.

2 · Node model, pinned to FDTD

κ(λ) extracted from the measured dn=0 MZI spectrum via s₀ = cos 4κ; effective phase length LP,eff = 23.70 μm (nominal 24, i.e. overlap Γ≈0.99) fit to the measured s(Δn) staircase — model rms 0.0038 across all nine FDTD points. Per-node power transmission 0.983.

3 · The mesh + delays IS a convolution (demo A)

Peak-sampled mesh outputs equal yi,t = Σj Uij st-j slot by slot. The error budget vs pulse width (right panel) is the design finding: the 16.4 fs compressed pulse carries 26.8 THz of bandwidth and samples both the coupler's κ(λ) drift and the newly measured per-node phase dispersion (−0.25°/nm, §6) — 0.8 bits. At 200 fs FWHM (guard ratio 2.5 in the 501 fs slot) the same mesh gives 6.6 bits. Compression buys slot RATE, not mixer accuracy: run the mixer with the longest pulse the guard band allows.

4 · It computes something useful as-is (demo B)

Program U = DFT5 and the mesh is a sliding 5-point DFT — a 2-THz-frame-rate spectrogram engine (this exact mixer is the FNet token-mixing layer). Any unitary gives an energy-conserving, perfectly-conditioned (κ=1, invertible) multi-head FIR mixer — the Hyena/S4 short-filter primitive with orthonormal heads.

5 · Attention: the structural gap, then the escape hatch (demos C, D)

Left: the best possible fixed linear (Toeplitz) operator fits a Hyena-style conv target exactly (R²=1.000000 — that IS this device) but tops out at R²≈0.95 on scalar self-attention and falls to 0.54 on generic vector-token attention (d=4, sharp softmax): content-dependent mixing is not in the linear span, at any N. Middle: the balanced-homodyne score head. The 45/55 coupler leaks an intensity-imbalance term (t²−r²)(|a|²−|b|²) worth 3.5% rms; subtracting the two single-arm balanced measurements (a real 3-measurement calibration) removes it exactly, leaving rms 4.0e-06 — the homodyne cross term is a perfect token product times one global constant because both arms share one pulse shape. Right: window-5 softmax attention closed through the chip: photonic scores, electronic softmax and reweight — indistinguishable from float.

Vector tokens come free: the master MRR is a comb source, so embedding dim c rides comb line c and the photodetector's sum over wavelength turns the score head into a true d-dimensional qt·kt-k per slot. Not simulated here (the calibration set covers 1470–1630 nm; a multi-line run is the natural next step).

6 · FDTD validation — and a discovery

Four new MEEP runs close the assumptions the envelope model makes. (1) Coherent two-input node. The calibrated MZI driven on both ports (relative phase 0° and 90°; the original calibration only drove one port). In-phase drive matches the model raw to 0.4–1%. Quadrature drive exposed what power-only calibration cannot see: a phase correction. A joint refit of ALL data at 1550 (9-point staircase + both runs) leaves κ unchanged (0.7368→0.7370), refines LP,eff 23.70→23.88 μm, and needs one static launch screen δ=−13° — total two-input rms 0.0043 at 1550 (raw 0.060), staircase rms improves to 0.0016. (2) The dispersion of that screen is real and lives in the MZI: sweeping wavelength, the quadrature screen slides at −0.25°/nm (≈6 fs of internal differential group delay); a single-coupler two-input control run shows ≈0 (+0.04°/nm), and a dn=0 MZI run reproduces the same slope with a different static offset (−50° at the full-cross set point, where quadrature sensitivity peaks). Consequence: per-node calibration is a static 2D LUT (set point × phase offset) at the operating wavelength — standard practice — but the λ-slope is NOT calibratable and is included in every OTDM number in this report (it is what kills the 16.4 fs operating point in §3). (3) Score head on real pulse trains in the real coupler geometry: 150 fs-slot scale model (labeled: slots compressed so the train fits the cell; pulse-interference physics is slot-spacing independent for non-overlapping pulses), 3-run leak-corrected balanced receiver — token products recovered to relative rms 6.4e-05.

8 · Compute density: the compact node vs a B300

Baseline: B300 = 15 PFLOPS dense FP4 = 7.5×1015 MAC/s on ~1650 mm² of dual-die silicon → 4.5×1012 MAC/s/mm² (die-level; the SXM module is much larger, so this denominator is conservative AGAINST us). Our density = slot rate / node footprint — both MACs and mesh area scale as N², so the levers are the node, the slot, and WDM.

The compact node (FDTD-recalibrated, not assumed): port pitch 6→4 μm (edge gap 3 μm: extrapolated Lπ≈0.4 m → <1% crosstalk over a mesh), s-bends 14→8 μm (min bend radius 9.7 μm; node T 0.975 vs 0.983 original — the tighter bends cost 0.8% and the cross state is cleaner, s₀=-0.9886), and the 24 μm phase arm replaced by a 6 μm trim stub — a fixed-weight mesh sets θ geometrically (arm-length offset; validated in FDTD: δL=0.30 μm → s = -0.038 measured vs +0.000 predicted). Node: 96.7→ 52.6 μm, footprint 580→210 μm² (2.8×). Compact-node quadrature phase screen: +0.10°/nm (vs −0.25 for the original), folded into the accuracy column.

Energy is NOT audited here (B300: 0.19 pJ/FLOP; an honest optical energy audit needs the comb power budget and is the known risk — flagged, not claimed).

9 · Optimization campaign (4 loops, adversarial critic)

Full log in OPTIMIZATION.md; each loop's methodology was adversarially reviewed by an independent critic agent whose findings set the next loop (results in out/opt_loop1..4.json). The noise question: inter-pulse overlap is real but is NOT guide dispersion (0.09 fs² of GDD over the delay ladder — zero); it is slot-tail overlap with a measured cliff when pulse FWHM exceeds ~0.4×slot, plus ~2.2 fs/node of phase-screen walk-off. With realistic control errors the budget flips entirely: coupler fab disorder (12 mrad) > phase-set/trim errors > overlap ISI > node dispersion > guide dispersion (nil). Key recoveries: the exact per-node- κ Clements compile (in-situ characterize each coupler to ≤5 mrad, then re-decompose) buys +1.0 bit and turns the dominant fab error into a calibration step; receiver choice is a TWO-way tie at spec (5.8±0.1 bits, N=5: gaussian-filtered/TL source with peak readout vs raw compressed pulses with a ±100-fs-tolerant gated pulsed-LO homodyne — the gate may be the easier hardware; NEVER ring filters, Lorentzian tails cost 3+ bits); comb linewidth ≤1 MHz suffices (real microcombs: ≲100 kHz). The honest Pareto: optical-in/optical-out layers would keep 579–2079× B300 die density at 4.0–5.8 bits (UNSIMULATED as chained layers — flagged); pricing full electronic readout (staggered pulsed-LO I/Q receiver banks — no 2-THz ADC exists) collapses density to 23–142×. Critic-4 verdicts, six standing HIGH caveats (incl.: no energy/power axis anywhere; composition never checked against full-wave; score floors are noiseless), and the verbatim residual-risk statement are in OPTIMIZATION.md. Trajectory: 7.2 bits (loop 1, naive) → 5.8±0.1 (loop 4, honest) — the number fell every time the model told fewer lies.

10 · How perfect, per amplitude

The system is strictly linear in field amplitude, so the meaningful question is where the ADDITIVE floors bite. Measured (full loop-4 error spec, κ-aware compile): relative accuracy is amplitude-flat — bits are identical for token scales A = 0.1 … 0.97 at every N (5.77/5.22/4.27 for N=5/8/16), because the dominant errors (coupler disorder, phase set, trim) are multiplicative and the crosstalk floor scales with the ensemble. Binned per amplitude LEVEL, slots whose window averages small |tokens| lose ≤0.2 bit to the additive floor (5.6 vs 5.8) — the ADC-style answer. The score head is flat at ~1.1e-5 relative across two decades of |product| under the full error model; the real-FDTD residuals bound the hardware floor at ~1e-4 (grid-limited). Data: out/amp_metrics.json, amp_metrics.py.

Methods & caveats

  • 2D slab physics throughout, inherited from the silica repo; no substrate leakage or roughness.
  • Mesh propagation is exact spectral-domain linear physics with the FDTD-pinned κ(λ), a(λ), 1/λ electrode phases; full-mesh FDTD is intractable (∼500×40 μm at res 25) — instead the two node-level assumptions are FDTD-checked (§6).
  • κ(λ) data cover 1470–1630 nm; the ±3 dB spectral tails of the 16.4 fs pulse reuse edge values (clamped interpolation). The long-pulse operating point never leaves the band.
  • The −0.25°/nm node phase dispersion is measured on ONE node geometry at two set points and applied identically to every mesh node (same geometry → same screen, worst-case coherent addition). Its microscopic origin (s-bend/coupler junction phase vs a residual FDTD launch systematic) is not fully resolved — the single-coupler control bounds the launch contribution at ≈6× smaller. Treating it as real is the conservative choice.
  • Token writing (EO serializer, ≤1 GHz electronics → N·B aggregate) is the silica repo's ladder result and is taken as given here; this build starts at "string of pulses with values on them".
  • Reading yt per slot at 2 THz is NOT claimed: outputs either stay optical (feed the next mixer/layer), are time-binned by slow detectors (spectrogram, scores averaged over frames), or are read at the electronics rate. The score head's per-slot products are consumed by the same slow softmax electronics that already frame-limit the loop.
  • Prior art honestly placed: delayed-replica photonic convolution is Xu et al., Nature 589, 44 (2021); photonic attention demos (2023–25) also route softmax through electronics. New here: the unitary (orthonormal-multi-head, invertible) tap bank via native-κ Clements decomposition, and the exactness of the leak-corrected homodyne score band on a measured imperfect coupler.
